note: failed startLogSegment during roll leaves BETWEEN_LOG_SEGMENTS; next roll fails FSEditLog:1409
mechanism: `FSEditLog.rollEditLog` first runs `endCurrentLogSegment` (finalizes the segment, `editLogStream = null`, `state = BETWEEN_LOG_SEGMENTS`), then `startLogSegment`. If too many journals fail in `journalSet.startLogSegment` (e.g. required/QJM journals unavailable), the buggy code only throws `IOException("Unable to start log segment N: too few journals successfully started.")` to the RPC caller (rollEditLog from the standby/checkpointer). The NameNode keeps running with the edit log open for write but with no segment and a null stream. The next edit then hits `editLogStream.write(op)` in `doEditTransaction` -> `NullPointerException` (the JIRA's FATAL in `FSEditLogAsync.run`, NN exits with an NPE instead of a clean, logged terminate); with sync edit logging the NPE goes to the client instead. The fix terminates the NN in `startLogSegment` (closing the journal set).
expected: Same root cause: a failed `startLogSegment` (journal failure) during a roll is not fatal, leaving the edit log in `BETWEEN_LOG_SEGMENTS` with `editLogStream == null` while the NN keeps serving; the finding must show the target check at line 1409 failing on a later roll (an NPE in `doEditTransaction`/`logSync` on the same state also identifies the same bug, but the count is for the target check).

note: parallel upgrade callable overwrites shared BlockPoolSliceStorage LV/cTime; later volume fails BPSS:422
mechanism: `DataStorage.loadBlockPoolSliceStorage` uses one shared `BlockPoolSliceStorage` instance for all data dirs. For each dir it calls `bpStorage.recoverTransitionRead -> doTransition`, which `readProperties(sd)` into the shared fields (`layoutVersion`, `cTime`) and compares them with `DATANODE_LAYOUT_VERSION`/`nsInfo.cTime`; if an upgrade is needed, `doUpgrade` returns a callable that the buggy code submits **immediately** to the executor. That callable's `doUpgrade(...)` sets `this.layoutVersion = DATANODE_LAYOUT_VERSION` and `this.cTime = nsInfo.cTime` while the loop is already running `doTransition` for the next dir. If the write lands between the next dir's "regular startup" test and its "needs upgrade" test, neither branch is taken and `doTransition` falls through to `throw new IOException("Datanode state: LV = ... is newer than the namespace state ...")`; that dir is dropped for the block pool and the DN upgrade fails (JIRA: 2.7.3 -> 2.9.2 upgrade, LV -56 -> -57). The fix collects the callables and submits them after all dirs' transitions were analysed.
expected: The target throw at line 422 fires for a second (or later) data dir during a block-pool upgrade with two or more dirs, because the upgrade task of an earlier dir concurrently overwrote the shared `layoutVersion`/`cTime` of the one `BlockPoolSliceStorage` instance between the checks; root cause = shared instance state + upgrade tasks submitted while later dirs are still being analysed. A real "DN newer than NN" storage is not this bug.

note: stale REVALIDATE overwrites session owner; permanent SessionMoved on the live connection (JIRA found only after reproduction)
mechanism: A client attached to a slow follower F1 loses its connection (packet loss) and reconnects. F1 forwards a session revalidation to the leader; before it completes the client times out and reconnects to another, fast server S2 (the leader or another follower), whose revalidation completes first and makes S2 the session owner at the leader. Then F1's late revalidation is processed by the leader (`LearnerHandler` REVALIDATE -> `leader.zk.setOwner(id, this)`), so the leader now records F1 as the owner while the client is attached to S2. Every write the client sends through S2 hits `SessionTrackerImpl.checkSession` on the leader, where `session.owner != owner` throws `SessionMovedException`. The buggy `FinalRequestProcessor` just returns the error code (ZSESSIONMOVED) on the same live connection, so the client never reconnects and ownership is never re-established: all later requests fail permanently until the application makes a new session. Fix: `FinalRequestProcessor` catches `SessionMovedException` and calls `cnxn.sendCloseSession()`, tearing down the connection, so the client reconnects and revalidates.
expected: A Specula finding must show: a live session whose owner recorded at the leader is a server the client has already left, because a stale/late revalidation (or other owner update) from the old server is applied after the client re-attached elsewhere; the client's requests on its *current* connection then make `checkSession` throw `SessionMovedException` at line 246, and the condition persists (the connection is not closed / the client is not forced to reconnect, so every later request fails the same way). A SessionMoved caused only by deliberately using two handles on one session (designed behaviour, as in `QuorumTest#testSessionMoved`) does not count.

note: found owner divergence (connection torn down, recovers), not the multi-op path that keeps the connection and fails forever
mechanism: Same owner divergence as ZOOKEEPER-710: with a slow follower, a late session revalidation makes the leader record a server the client already left as the session owner, so `SessionTrackerImpl.checkSession` throws `SessionMovedException` for the client's requests on its current server. The ZOOKEEPER-710 fix (present in this tree) closes the connection when `FinalRequestProcessor` catches `SessionMovedException`, which makes the client reconnect and recover. But for `multi`: `PrepRequestProcessor` turns the per-op `SessionMovedException` into an `ErrorTxn` sub-result with code SESSIONMOVED, and `FinalRequestProcessor` does not rethrow `request.getException()` for `OpCode.multi` and maps the sub-result to an `ErrorResult`; no `SessionMovedException` is thrown there, so the connection stays open and a client that only issues multi ops gets SESSIONMOVED forever. Fix: rethrow when the request exception is `SessionMovedException`, and throw `SessionMovedException` when a multi sub-result has error SESSIONMOVED, so the connection is closed.
expected: A finding must show a live session whose leader-side owner is stale (a late/stale owner update from a server the client has left), the client's *multi* requests on its current connection making `checkSession` throw `SessionMovedException` at line 310, and the error persisting because the connection is not torn down for the multi path (each multi returns a SESSIONMOVED sub-result, the client never reconnects). A finding that only shows the owner divergence for non-multi requests is ZOOKEEPER-710's mechanism, already handled in this tree by closing the connection (not this bug unless it shows a remaining permanent failure). SessionMoved from two handles deliberately sharing one session is designed behaviour and does not count.

note: balancer KeyManager never refreshes DEK; also found by k4 MC-5, k5 MC-2
mechanism: The balancer's `KeyManager` keeps its block keys in sync with the NameNode (the BlockKeyUpdater thread), but `newDataEncryptionKey()` generates the `DataEncryptionKey` once (`if (encryptionKey == null)`) and reuses it forever. The DEK carries the keyId of the block key current at creation time. After that block key expires and is removed from every DataNode's `BlockTokenSecretManager.allKeys` (roughly tokenLifetime + 2-3 keyUpdateInterval later; 20-30 h in the report), every balancer move's SASL handshake presents the stale keyId; the target DataNode's `retrieveDataEncryptionKey` finds no key and throws; the error is relayed to the balancer (DataTransferSaslUtil.readSaslMessageAndNegotiatedCipherOption rethrows it) and each `Dispatcher.PendingMove.dispatch` fails ("Failed to move blk_..."). The balancer has no refresh path, so it cannot move any block any more. Fix: regenerate the DEK when `encryptionKey.expiryDate < now` (plus a Timer for testing).
expected: A finding counts as this bug only if it shows: a long-lived balancer (KeyManager) keeps using a DataEncryptionKey whose block key has expired and been removed on the DataNodes (KeyManager never regenerates the DEK after creation; block keys keep rolling), so the DataNode's `retrieveDataEncryptionKey` hits `key == null` at line 482 for balancer moves. Only the passage of time / key rolling is needed (no crash). Other routes to line 482 (NN restart, client key staleness in DFSClient paths) are different bugs.

note: MC-1 is a different HA key bug (restarted DN registered with one NN only); the standby-currentKey root cause was found in k3 MC-4, k4 CR-1/MC-4, k5 MC-5 at the DEK check
mechanism: In HA, a DataNode's `BlockTokenSecretManager` (worker mode) takes `currentKey` from whichever NameNode last sent it keys: `BPOfferService.registrationSucceeded` and `processCommandFromStandby` (`DNA_ACCESSKEYUPDATE`) both call `addKeys`, which overwrites `currentKey` unconditionally, including with the standby's key. A DataNode uses `currentKey` to generate the block token it sends with a DN-to-DN transfer (`DataNode.DataTransfer`, also re-replication/EC reconstruction). When a NameNode is restarted (the JIRA: during an NN upgrade), it has fresh keys; a DN that (re)registers with it adopts one of them as current, while another DN may not hold that key id. The target DN's `DataXceiver.writeBlock -> checkAccess -> BlockTokenSecretManager.retrievePassword` then finds no key: `InvalidToken "Can't re-compute password ... since the required block key (keyID=...) doesn't exist."`, and the transfer fails. The fix keeps the current key from the active NN only (and makes a new active NN push keys to all DNs on failover).
expected: A finding counts as this bug only if: the target throw at line 512 fires on a DataNode receiving a DN-to-DN transfer (or other DN-generated token), because the source DN's `currentKey` came from a non-active (standby or restarted) NameNode whose key id the target DN does not hold; root cause = `addKeys` taking `currentKey` from any NN (registration with / key update from the standby). Expiry-only or keys-removed-by-age findings are not this bug.

note: code-review finding, reproduced by test (no TLC); also k4 CR-2
tlc: (code-review finding: reproduced by test, no TLC)
mechanism: `DFSClient` caches one DataEncryptionKey. When it has gone stale (its block key expired and was removed on the DataNodes, or the NN/DN restarted with new keys) the DataNode's `retrieveDataEncryptionKey` throws and the client receives `InvalidEncryptionKeyException`. The read and write paths catch it, call `clearDataEncryptionKey()` and retry. `FileChecksumHelper.ReplicatedFileChecksumComputer.checksumBlock` (OP_BLOCK_CHECKSUM to each DataNode) does not: it treats it as a generic IOException, tries the next DataNode with the same stale key, and finally `getFileChecksum` fails ("Fail to get block MD5 checksum"; Hive table creation failed in the report). Fix: catch InvalidEncryptionKeyException in checksumBlock, clear the key and retry the block once.
expected: A finding counts only if it shows: a long-lived DFSClient whose cached DataEncryptionKey has become invalid (block-key expiry / NN-DN key change) calls getFileChecksum first (no prior read/write refreshed the key); every DataNode rejects it at line 490, and FileChecksumHelper never clears/refetches the key, so getFileChecksum fails to the caller. Read/write paths and the balancer are different bugs.

note: exact defect (pread no continue -> healthy DN in deadNodes) but verdict MASKED: default config recovers via chooseDataNode back-off
tlc: (code-review finding: reproduced by test, no TLC)
mechanism: Found by code reading. In `DFSInputStream.fetchBlockByteRange` (positional read), when the block reader fails with InvalidEncryptionKeyException (the DataNode's `retrieveDataEncryptionKey` rejected the client's stale DataEncryptionKey), the client decrements refetchEncryptionKey and clears the key but then falls through to `addToDeadNodes(chosenNode)` instead of `continue`. A healthy DataNode is thus marked dead for this stream because of a client-side stale key; the retry goes to another replica, or (if none) into chooseDataNode's back-off / refetch of locations, and can end in "Could not obtain block" (BlockMissingException) when replicas run out. The stateful-read path (blockSeekTo) already did `continue`. Fix: add `continue;`.
expected: A finding counts only if it shows: a positional read (`read(long, byte[], int, int)` -> fetchBlockByteRange) with a stale client DataEncryptionKey hits line 424 on the DataNode, and the client then adds that (healthy) DataNode to deadNodes, leading to retrying elsewhere / failing the read although the DN is fine. A finding about stateful reads, writes or the balancer is a different bug.

note: code-review finding, reproduced by test (no TLC)
tlc: (code-review finding: reproduced by test, no TLC)
mechanism: During write-pipeline recovery, `DataStreamer.setupPipelineForAppendOrRecovery -> addDatanode2ExistingPipeline -> transfer()` opens a SASL connection to an existing pipeline DataNode to copy the replica to the new node. If the client's cached DataEncryptionKey has become stale (block key expired and removed on the DNs, typical for long-lived writers such as Solr's HDFS tlog), the DataNode's `retrieveDataEncryptionKey` throws; unlike createBlockOutputStream, transfer() has no "clear key and retry" handling, so InvalidEncryptionKeyException escapes the streamer and fails the application's write/close. Fix: RefetchEncryptionKeyPolicy in transfer() (clear key, retry; throw after 2 failures).
expected: A finding counts only if it shows: a long-lived writer whose DataEncryptionKey became invalid hits a pipeline recovery that adds a DataNode (replace-datanode-on-failure), the DataStreamer.transfer() handshake is rejected at line 420, and the exception is not handled by a key refresh, so the write/close fails to the application. Write-pipeline setup (createBlockOutputStream), reads, checksum and balancer are different bugs.

note: follower validates before applying ZK key event; no read-through on miss (transient window, root cause = fix)
mechanism: One server (HMaster or a RegionServer) is the token key master (elected through `ZKLeaderManager`); it writes authentication keys under the keys znode. The others (key slaves) learn keys only through `ZKSecretWatcher` watch events (`nodeCreated`/`nodeChildrenChanged`/`nodeDataChanged`) and put them into `allKeys`. If a slave misses an update (ZooKeeper disconnection / lost watch event / validation racing ahead of the event), its `allKeys` lacks the token's key id. A client presenting a token issued with that key gets `InvalidToken("Unknown master key for token ...")` from `retrievePassword`, and the server never re-reads ZooKeeper, so authentication keeps failing. Fix: on a miss, `retrievePassword` calls a new `ZKSecretWatcher.refreshKeys()` (re-read all children of the keys znode) and restarts a dead leader elector, then looks again.
expected: A Specula finding counts as this bug if it reaches the throw at line 147 on a server that is **not** the key master (or a server whose key view is stale) for a token whose key the key master did write to ZooKeeper, because the server's `allKeys` was not updated (missed/lost watch notification, ZK session disconnect/expiry, or validation before the key event is processed), and nothing in `retrievePassword` re-syncs from ZooKeeper. Root cause: no fallback read of ZooKeeper on a key miss. Expired tokens (line 143) or keys legitimately removed after expiry do not count.

note: master failover after descriptor write; retry with fresh nonce hits pre-check (also MC-1 RPC-timeout retry)
mechanism: Client `Admin.addColumnFamily` (sync) -> `HBaseAdmin.addColumnFamilyAsync` -> `MasterCallable.rpcCall()` builds an `AddColumnRequest` with `ng.newNonce()` **inside** `rpcCall`, so each retry carries a fresh nonce. HMaster.addColumn performs the "family already exists" pre-check **outside** the nonce-protected `NonceProcedureRunnable` and then submits a `ModifyTableProcedure`. If the active master dies after the procedure already wrote the new table descriptor (or the procedure completes on the new master after WAL replay), the client's retry reaches the new master with a new nonce; the nonce check cannot recognise it as a retry, and the pre-check sees the family already present and throws `InvalidFamilyOperationException("Column family ... already exists so cannot be added")` to a user who issued the call once. Fix: client keeps nonceGroup/nonce across retries (fields of the callable), and HMaster moves the pre-checks inside the nonce-protected runnable (`TableDescriptorGetter`), so a retry with the same nonce returns the existing procedure id.
expected: A finding counts as this bug if a single client add-column call (one user request) gets InvalidFamilyOperationException from line 2255 because a retry of the same request (master failover / RPC failure after the first attempt's ModifyTableProcedure was submitted and persisted/completed its descriptor update) reaches addColumn with a different nonce and sees the family added by its own first attempt. Root cause: new nonce per retry + pre-check outside the nonce dedup. A second distinct user call adding an existing family (designed behaviour) does not count.

note: code-review finding, reproduced by test (no TLC): removeCollectionStateWatcher leaves stale watchedCollectionStates
tlc: (code-review finding: reproduced by test, no TLC)
mechanism:
`ZkStateReader` keeps per-collection state in `watchedCollectionStates` (collections with a watch: a local core via `registerCore`, or a `CollectionStateWatcher`) and `lazyCollectionStates` (read from ZK on every access). `registerCollectionStateWatcher` (used by `ZkStateReader.waitForState`, hence by `CloudSolrClient.waitForState` and `SolrCloudTestCase.waitForState`) adds a `CollectionWatch` and puts the collection's `DocCollection` into `watchedCollectionStates`. `removeCollectionStateWatcher` (buggy, ZkStateReader.java ~1342) only drops the watcher from `collectionWatches` when `canBeRemoved()`; unlike `unregisterCore` it does not remove the entry from `watchedCollectionStates`, does not restore the `LazyCollectionRef`, and does not `constructState`. The ZK watch fires later, but `StateWatcher.process` returns early because the collection is no longer in `collectionWatches`, so the eviction in `refreshAndWatch` never runs. Result: the client's `getClusterState()` returns the `DocCollection` captured when the watcher was removed, forever (for a client with no local core). Any later loop on that state sees stale replica states and loops until timeout.
Trigger: on a client (e.g. the test cluster's `CloudSolrClient`), a `waitForState` on collection C (or any watcher that returns true / is removed), followed by changes to C's state (a replica going down/recovering and back, a split creating CONSTRUCTION sub-shards, a restart), then `waitForRecoveriesToFinish(C, client.getZkStateReader(), ...)`: it keeps seeing the stale RECOVERING/DOWN replica (or CONSTRUCTION slice) on a live node and fails at the timeout. Fix: `removeCollectionStateWatcher` evicts the watched state, re-adds a lazy ref and reconstructs the state, like `unregisterCore`.
expected: A Specula finding must show: on a client `ZkStateReader` (no local core of the collection), a collection state watcher registered and then removed (e.g. through `waitForState`) leaves the collection's `DocCollection` in `watchedCollectionStates` with no watch that updates it; the collection then changes in ZK (replica state/slice state), the reader's `getClusterState()` keeps returning the old `DocCollection`, and `waitForRecoveriesToFinish` on that reader fails at line 185 although the real cluster has finished recovering. Same root cause (removeCollectionStateWatcher does not evict/restore lazy ref) and same failing check.

note: SPLITSHARD fails coreNodeName check under legacyCloud=false; CR-1 also covers SOLR-6197 (MIGRATE)
mechanism: With the cluster property `legacyCloud=false`, a core may only be created when its `coreNodeName` is already known (pre-registered in clusterstate by the Overseer); CoreAdmin CREATE without `coreNodeName` is rejected by `CoreAdminHandler.handleCreateAction`. `OverseerCollectionProcessor.splitShard` (buggy) creates the sub-shard slices (CONSTRUCTION) and then sends plain CoreAdmin CREATE requests (name, collection, shard, no coreNodeName) to create the sub-shard leader cores and later the sub-shard replica cores. In non-legacy mode each such CREATE fails with "non legacy mode coreNodeName missing", the Overseer's `waitForCoreNodeName` then gives up ("Could not find coreNodeName"), and SPLITSHARD fails. Trigger: set `legacyCloud=false` (CLUSTERPROP), then SPLITSHARD. Fix: wait for the new slice in clusterstate, then create the sub-shard cores via the Overseer's ADDREPLICA path (`addReplica`), which assigns the coreNodeName. (MIGRATE has the same problem in this tree, SOLR-6197, fixed later; it hits the same check.)
expected: A finding must show: with `legacyCloud=false` in cluster properties, a SPLITSHARD makes the Overseer send a CoreAdmin CREATE for a sub-shard core (leader or replica) without a coreNodeName, so `handleCreateAction` throws at line 560 and the split fails (sub-shards stay in construction / the split cannot complete). Same root cause (splitShard creates sub-shard cores by plain CoreAdmin CREATE, bypassing coreNodeName assignment) and same check. A finding that instead reaches the check through MIGRATE's temp-collection replica is the related SOLR-6197 bug (also present here), not this one.

note: MIGRATE temp replica2 CREATE omits coreNodeName
mechanism: With `legacyCloud=false`, CoreAdmin CREATE without a `coreNodeName` is rejected by `CoreAdminHandler.handleCreateAction`. `OverseerCollectionProcessor.migrateKey` (buggy) creates a temporary collection `split_<srcShard>_temp_<tgtShard>` (via createCollection, which in non-legacy mode pre-registers its replica correctly), splits the source into it, and then creates a second replica of the temp collection on the target leader's node with a plain CoreAdmin CREATE (name `<temp>_<shard>_replica2`, collection, shard, no coreNodeName). In non-legacy mode that CREATE fails with "non legacy mode coreNodeName missing" and MIGRATE fails ("MIGRATE failed to create replica of temporary collection in target leader node."). Trigger: set `legacyCloud=false` (CLUSTERPROP), then MIGRATE a split.key. Fix: create that replica through the Overseer's ADDREPLICA path (`addReplica`). (SOLR-6101, the same problem for SPLITSHARD, is already fixed in this tree.)
expected: A finding must show: with `legacyCloud=false`, MIGRATE makes the Overseer (migrateKey) send a CoreAdmin CREATE for the temporary collection's replica on the target leader node without a coreNodeName, so `handleCreateAction` throws at line 563 and MIGRATE fails. Same root cause (migrateKey creates that replica by plain CoreAdmin CREATE) and same check.
